atoms.text: This guide configures the ClipForge transcoding workers to read mezzanine video files from the bucket acme-media-masters and write encoded renditions back to the same bucket. The workers run under the IAM role ClipForgeTranscodeRole in account 111122223333. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to this role, and the bucket policy is left unchanged. Create a policy with one statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-masters/masters/* and a second statement that allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-masters/renditions/*. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-masters with an s3:prefix condition of masters/ so the workers can enumerate pending jobs. Attach the policy to ClipForgeTranscodeRole with the IAM console or the attach-role-policy command. Confirm that Block Public Access remains enabled on the bucket, since no bucket-level change is required. Submit a test job and verify that the rendition appears under renditions/ and that a write attempt under masters/ is denied.

This guide configures the ClipForge transcoding workers to read mezzanine video files from the bucket acme-media-masters and write encoded renditions back to the same bucket. The workers run under the IAM role ClipForgeTranscodeRole in account 111122223333. Access is granted only through statements in the bucket's resource-based policy, and no S3 permissions are attached to the role itself. Add a statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ClipForgeTranscodeRole and that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-masters/masters/*, then add a second statement for the same Principal that allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-masters/renditions/*. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-masters with an s3:prefix condition of masters/ so the workers can enumerate pending jobs. Save the policy with the put-bucket-policy command or the Permissions tab, keeping any existing statements. Confirm that Block Public Access remains enabled, since a statement naming a single role ARN does not make the bucket public. Submit a test job and verify that the rendition appears under renditions/ and that a write attempt under masters/ is denied.

This guide gives an on-premises PDF text-extraction batch job access to the bucket acme-scans-inbox. The job authenticates as the IAM user docparse-batch, which uses a long-term access key stored in the job's credentials file. It reads scanned PDFs from the incoming/ prefix and writes extracted text as JSON files to the extracted/ prefix. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to docparse-batch, and the bucket policy is not modified. The policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-inbox/incoming/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-inbox/extracted/*. It also allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-inbox restricted to the incoming/ prefix. Attach the policy with the put-user-policy command or the IAM console, then run aws s3 ls from the batch host to confirm the listing works. Process one sample PDF and confirm that the JSON output is created under extracted/.

This guide gives an on-premises PDF text-extraction batch job access to the bucket acme-scans-inbox. The job authenticates as the IAM user docparse-batch, which uses a long-term access key stored in the job's credentials file. It reads scanned PDFs from the incoming/ prefix and writes extracted text as JSON files to the extracted/ prefix. Access is granted only by statements in the bucket's resource-based policy, and docparse-batch has no S3 permissions in its own identity policies. The bucket policy statement uses arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/docparse-batch as the Principal and allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-inbox/incoming/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-inbox/extracted/*. A further statement for the same Principal allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-inbox restricted to the incoming/ prefix. Apply the policy with the put-bucket-policy command or the console, then run aws s3 ls from the batch host to confirm the listing works. Process one sample PDF and confirm that the JSON output is created under extracted/.

This procedure lets the PixelSizer thumbnail service read uploaded photographs and write resized copies in the bucket customer-uploads-images. The service runs under the IAM role PixelSizerRole in account 111122223333. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy on this role, and the bucket policy stays as it is. The policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::customer-uploads-images/originals/*. It also allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::customer-uploads-images/thumbnails/*, with a condition that requires the s3:x-amz-acl header to be absent so objects keep the bucket's default ownership settings. Delete permissions are intentionally omitted, so the service cannot remove original files. Attach the policy to PixelSizerRole and start the service with that role. Upload a test JPEG to originals/ and check that three thumbnail sizes appear under thumbnails/.

The service runs under the IAM role PixelSizerRole in account 111122223333. Access is granted only through statements in the bucket's resource-based policy, and the role carries no S3 permissions of its own. One statement names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/PixelSizerRole as the Principal and allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::customer-uploads-images/originals/*. A second statement for the same Principal allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::customer-uploads-images/thumbnails/*, with a condition that requires the s3:x-amz-acl header to be absent so objects keep the bucket's default ownership settings. Delete permissions are intentionally omitted, so the service cannot remove original files. Save the policy to the bucket and start the service with that role. Upload a test JPEG to originals/ and check that three thumbnail sizes appear under thumbnails/.

This guide grants the LevelMeter audio normalization service access to the bucket acme-podcast-audio. The service reads uncompressed WAV recordings from the raw/ prefix and writes loudness-normalized MP3 files to the normalized/ prefix. It runs under the IAM role LevelMeterRole in account 111122223333. The grant is made only in an identity-based policy attached to LevelMeterRole, and the bucket policy is not edited. Write a policy that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::acme-podcast-audio/raw/*, since the bucket has versioning enabled. Add a statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-podcast-audio/normalized/*. Attach the policy to the role and restart the service so it picks up the new permissions. Process a sample episode and confirm that the MP3 file appears under normalized/ and the WAV file in raw/ is unchanged.

This guide grants the LevelMeter audio normalization service access to the bucket acme-podcast-audio. The service reads uncompressed WAV recordings from the raw/ prefix and writes loudness-normalized MP3 files to the normalized/ prefix. It runs under the IAM role LevelMeterRole in account 111122223333. The grant is made only in the bucket's resource-based policy, and no S3 permissions are added to LevelMeterRole. Add a statement with arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/LevelMeterRole as the Principal that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::acme-podcast-audio/raw/*, since the bucket has versioning enabled. Add a statement for the same Principal that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-podcast-audio/normalized/*. Apply the bucket policy and restart the service so it uses the role with the updated bucket configuration. Process a sample episode and confirm that the MP3 file appears under normalized/ and the WAV file in raw/ is unchanged.

This guide sets up an OCR pipeline in which the service reads archived page images from one bucket and writes searchable text output to a second bucket. The source bucket is acme-records-archive and the destination bucket is acme-ocr-output. The workers run under the IAM role OcrWorkerRole in account 111122223333. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to the role, and neither bucket policy is changed. The policy gives read-only access, s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket, on acme-records-archive and its objects. A separate statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-ocr-output/text/*. Because there is no write action on the archive bucket, the workers cannot alter the source images. Attach the policy to OcrWorkerRole and run a test job on one TIFF file. Check that the text file is created under text/ in acme-ocr-output.

This guide sets up an OCR pipeline in which the service reads archived page images from one bucket and writes searchable text output to a second bucket. The source bucket is acme-records-archive and the destination bucket is acme-ocr-output. The workers run under the IAM role OcrWorkerRole in account 111122223333. Access is granted only through resource-based policies on the two buckets, and the role has no S3 permissions attached. The policy on acme-records-archive names arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/OcrWorkerRole as the Principal and gives read-only access, s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket, on the bucket and its objects. The policy on acme-ocr-output has a statement for the same Principal that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-ocr-output/text/*. Because there is no write action in the archive bucket policy, the workers cannot alter the source images. Apply both bucket policies and run a test job on one TIFF file. Check that the text file is created under text/ in acme-ocr-output.

This guide provides the CaptionLine subtitle generator with access to the bucket acme-broadcast-ingest. The generator is a scheduled process that authenticates as the IAM user captionline-svc. It reads extracted audio tracks in FLAC format from the episodes/ prefix and writes WebVTT caption files to the subtitles/ prefix. The grant is made only in an identity-based policy attached to captionline-svc, and the bucket policy is not touched. The policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-broadcast-ingest/episodes/*.flac. It also allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-broadcast-ingest/subtitles/*.vtt, which prevents the process from writing other file types. Attach the policy with the IAM console or the put-user-policy command. Run the scheduled process manually once and confirm that a .vtt file is created next to the matching episode identifier under subtitles/.

This guide provides the CaptionLine subtitle generator with access to the bucket acme-broadcast-ingest. The generator is a scheduled process that authenticates as the IAM user captionline-svc. It reads extracted audio tracks in FLAC format from the episodes/ prefix and writes WebVTT caption files to the subtitles/ prefix. The grant is made only in the bucket's resource-based policy, and captionline-svc has no identity-based S3 permissions. A statement with arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/captionline-svc as the Principal allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-broadcast-ingest/episodes/*.flac. A second statement for the same Principal allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-broadcast-ingest/subtitles/*.vtt, which prevents the process from writing other file types. Add both statements with the console or the put-bucket-policy command. Run the scheduled process manually once and confirm that a .vtt file is created nextto the matching episode identifier under subtitles/.

This guide configures the MarkStamp watermarking service to read original photographs and write watermarked copies in the bucket acme-stock-photos. The service runs under the IAM role MarkStampRole in account 111122223333. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to MarkStampRole, and the bucket policy remains unchanged. The policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-stock-photos/originals/*. A second statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-stock-photos/watermarked/*, with a condition that requires the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header to equal AES256. Requests that omit the header are rejected, so the service must set it on every upload. Attach the policy to the role and set the encryption header in the service's upload configuration. Submit a test image and confirm that the watermarked copy appears under watermarked/ with server-side encryption enabled.

This guide gives the legacy DocConvert worker access to the bucket acme-contracts-docs for converting word-processor files to PDF. The worker runs on a fixed server and authenticates as the IAM user docconvert-legacy. It reads DOCX files from the drafts/ prefix and writes the converted PDF files to the final/ prefix. Some output files exceed 100 MB, so the worker uploads them using multipart upload. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to docconvert-legacy, and the bucket policy is not changed. The policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-contracts-docs/drafts/*. It also allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::acme-contracts-docs/final/*. Attach the policy to the user and update the worker's configuration with the user's current access key. Convert a large test document and confirm that the PDF appears under final/ and no incomplete multipart uploads remain.
